test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Machinist) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a major effect of a collision in a CNC machining centre?

options.text: Increased machine downtime and repair costs

solution:
The correct answer is __Increased machine downtime and repair costs.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A collision in a CNC machining centre can result in significant damage to the machine components.
 
• This leads to increased machine downtime as repairs and part replacements are necessary.
 
• High repair costs are incurred due to the specialized nature of CNC components and the precision required for repairs.
 
• Collisions can also damage the tools, fixtures, and workpieces, further increasing expenses.
 
• Preventive measures, such as collision detection systems, are often implemented to minimize such occurrences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Automatic correction of machining errors:**

 
 
• While some CNC systems may have error detection, automatic correction of machining errors is not a direct effect of a collision.
 
 
 
• **Enhanced efficiency in CNC operations:**
 
 
• Collisions reduce operational efficiency as they disrupt the production process and cause delays.
 
 
 
• **Improved tool performance and longevity:**
 
 
• Collisions damage tools and significantly shorten their lifespan, rather than improving performance.
